seatDelta2.coordinatorStatementReview: 2026-11-14, the coordinator's source review of committed-operations.ts at 106f22fa93838da816904ec2b7b72f7d90e38f0d: generationOf runs, inside the transaction of a request's first committed insert, the newest committed DatabaseRestored among rows with profile IS NULL, by json_extract on each. It cannot fail a write (guarded twice: its own try/catch and noteCommitted's) and it writes nothing, so it does not touch atomicity: accepted on that ground. Cost was raised (the statement scans every profile IS NULL row when no restore exists).
seatDelta2.statementNow: At ec16d45d, for the coordinator to read: committed-operations.ts:129 (generationOf's SELECT) runs inside the write transaction only from committed-operations.ts:102, the first note of a request that classified no Profile before writing (owner-only AuthChanged writes: setupOwner, resetPassphrase, issueToken, revokeToken, signOut), once per request and database. Every other writing request notes the generation its Profile classification already read inside the same transaction (auth.ts:791, noteGeneration, no SQL); the restore notes the generation it starts (store/snapshots.ts:588, no SQL). The settle reads no generation: committed-operations.ts:187 is an index range scan (op_log_profile_seq, profile IS NULL AND seq >= the request's first noted seq) run after the request, outside any transaction; it cannot throw out (try/catch: a failure means nothing is reported) and writes nothing. Measured on 50,000 profile IS NULL rows: generationOf 9.7 ms median (0.55 ms at 5,000), with or without a restore far back; the settle's scan 0.001 ms.
